# `silk/bench/report`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Turns the raw samples of a benchmark run into the report a renderer draws.

## When to use
Call [`Reports.make`](#Reports.impl.make) on a `silk.bench.record.RunResult` you read from a result file, to
render a saved run again or with another noise threshold. `silk.bench.bench` calls it for
every suite it runs.

## Details
A combination of parameters whose programs print result lines gets one table for each name
the lines carry, in the unit of the lines: `ns/op` when a line has it, or else the first
unit written. The medians of the other units are in the row. Where a larger value is better,
as for `req/s`, a ratio above 1 has the verdict `faster`. When the lines of two
implementations carry different checks for one name, the table is marked and no row of it
has a ratio. Every other combination gets one table of process times, as follows.

Each implementation gets one row for each benchmark. The row's statistics cover the measured
runs that exited with status 0: warm-up runs and failed runs are left out, and failed runs
are counted in the row. Every row except the reference's gets its ratio to the reference
with a 95% interval and a verdict, from `silk.bench.statistics`. A suite with more than one
benchmark also gets the geometric mean of each implementation's ratios.

Import as `Reports` with `import silk.bench.report { Reports }`.

<a id="Reports.impl.compared"></a>

### Associated function `compared`

```silk
pub effect fn compared(result: &mut RunResult, earlier: RunResult, label: string) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds the implementations of the earlier run `earlier` to `result` under the name `label`,
with their samples for the benchmarks both runs have, and makes the earlier reference the
reference. An earlier run with one implementation adds it as `label`; one with several
adds each as `<label>:<name>`. Returns `false`, and adds nothing, if `result` already has
an implementation named `label`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the names.

<a id="Reports.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make(result: &RunResult, noise: f64) -> Report
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the report of `result`, with verdicts at the noise threshold `noise`, a fraction
such as 0.01 for 1%.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the report.
